**Summary**  
The GNN-A model estimates a 45.7% risk of stage III–IV disease for C3N-01178. The prediction is driven primarily by tumor-protein features (81% share), led by extreme upregulation of HSD17B7 (cholesterol biosynthesis, ER membrane) and downregulation of GULP1, with a smaller contribution from the patient’s recorded hypertension (19% share). The tumor carries a somatic VHL frameshift (p.R177fs), the canonical ccRCC driver, and an RPL22 mutation. Model-ranked drugs include the proteasome inhibitor carfilzomib and the SYK inhibitor fostamatinib; model-ranked genes highlight nucleotide-metabolism and DNA-repair factors (PNP, FAN1, MPG).

**Evidence paths**  
- Patient has somatic VHL p.R177fs and RPL22 p.D35Y mutations [pt:C3N-01178:somatic_mutation:NCBIGene:7428][pt:C3N-01178:somatic_mutation:NCBIGene:6146].  
- HSD17B7 is the most up-regulated tumor protein (z=14.9) and the top tumor driver of risk (score 0.183) [pt:C3N-01178:protein_up:NCBIGene:51478][contrib:C3N-01178:NCBIGene:51478].  
- GULP1 is the most down-regulated protein (z=−12.2) and the second tumor driver (score 0.172) [pt:C3N-01178:protein_down:NCBIGene:51454][contrib:C3N-01178:NCBIGene:51454].  
- Hypertension phenotype contributes 0.225 as a clinical driver (18.6% share) [pt:C3N-01178:has_phenotype:HP:0000822][contrib:C3N-01178:HP:0000822].  
- HSD17B7 localizes to the endoplasmic reticulum membrane and participates in cholesterol biosynthesis [E3571897][E3811665].
